correctness.rationale: An edge-open-packing component is an induced star, so selecting leaves gives an independent set of size equal to the edge set. Every rung contributes at most one independent vertex, forcing at most n edges. Equality forces exactly one of two checkerboards. Star centres cover checkerboard leaves via indexed radius-one intervals; the intervals must partition rung indices. Boundary tiles of size two and interior tiles of size three give one interval cover in residue classes 0,1 modulo 3 and two in residue class 2; the other checkerboard doubles the count without duplication. Every n>=2 admits these covers, with the n=2 coinciding boundary intervals correctly distinguished by centre. A separately written C++17 exhaustive verifier tests every nonempty endpoint subset for n=2..11 (5,592,390 total), finding exact equality and enumerator counts. Infinite theorem follows from the proof.

value.rationale: This determines an entire natural infinite-family of optimizer structures for a recent combinatorial edge-packing problem. The optimum does not merely equal an existing independence bound: all extrema admit a unique indexed-interval description, and their total number exhibits a nontrivial periodic rigidity (2 or 4 regardless of ladder length). The phenomenon is a motivated instance in Cartesian-product graphs and test bed for related exact extremal and dynamic-programming methods. General inequalities, source algorithms and equivalences are not claimed as new.
